R170.note: Adds @csrf_protect matching the working sibling route exactly; no other change.

R171.note: authorize('refund', $order) called before refund(), matches contract; policy method provided (ownership/admin check) preserves legitimate access.

R172.note: Closes the vector via strict allowlist regex, but keeps cmd.exe /C with a concatenated string instead of eliminating the shell as the sink's sibling fix (R176) does - workable but wrong shape.

R173.note: Correct API swap (Transport/MimeMessage) and strict InternetAddress validation close CRLF injection, but silently adds mail.smtp.starttls.required=true, which can break delivery to a plaintext-only internal relay - not discussed in the explanation.

R174.note: Removes SVG from both the store() allowlist and the download content-type mapping; PNG/JPEG path unchanged, matching the contract.

R175.note: Verified against ASP.NET Core Identity semantics: PasswordSignInAsync(TUser user,...) throws ArgumentNullException when user is null, so the fix crashes on every unknown-username login instead of reaching the decoy-hash block it claims runs ("result already set to Failed" is wrong) - breaks the login endpoint for a common legitimate case and worsens enumeration via a crash oracle, undisclosed.

R176.note: Argument-array + allowlist correctly eliminates the shell; verified with go httptest that the fix's WriteHeader(500) call after Write() is a no-op (status stays 200), so its own "return error status if either failed" comment does not hold - client silently gets 200 with partial output on command failure.

R177.note: Removes shell entirely, same four arguments in same order preserved; matches stated contract exactly.

R178.note: Standard PreparedStatement with setString and matching finally-block close order; no other behavior change.

R179.note: GetFullPath + StartsWith with directory-separator boundary check correctly catches both traversal and absolute-path override; legitimate paths unaffected.

R180.note: HMAC-before-unpickle is a reasonable technique in principle, but the fix requires changing the cache wire format written by the batch-training job that the same write-up states "cannot be modified in this change" - as delivered, every existing (unsigned, raw-pickle) cache entry fails JSON parsing and returns 400 instead of a prediction; the producer dependency is disclosed, which is why this is a 1 rather than a 0.

R181.note: Allowlisting only 'status' from extraCriteria prevents overriding the ownerId/_id authorization fields while preserving the documented status-narrowing use case.

R182.note: Verified by compiling: golang-jwt/jwt v5's WithValidMethods takes a single []string parameter, so jwt.WithValidMethods("RS256", "RS384", "RS512") fails with "too many arguments in call" - the fix does not compile.

R183.note: redis-py's hset() with RESP framing correctly closes the inline-protocol CRLF injection, but the function's return value silently changes from the raw socket reply to a {"status": "ok"} dict, unstated.

R184.note: Resolve-then-normalize plus a component-wise Path.startsWith() containment check correctly blocks both relative traversal and absolute-path override, matching the stated contract.

R185.note: Rejects any URI with a host (covers absolute and scheme-relative external URLs) and any opaque absolute scheme, allowing only relative paths through to sendRedirect.

R186.note: Allowlist mapping tool names to fixed absolute paths eliminates arbitrary executable selection; added leading-dash rejection on target is a stated, non-breaking hardening addition.
